proposed_comments.title: Skip unchanged repeated key-down events before conflict handling
proposed_comments.body:
### Skip unchanged repeated key-down events before conflict handling

**Severity:** `high`

The current guard only suppresses the `Keys` assignment. When the user holds the same non-modifier or Windows key, `Hotkey_KeyDown` still clears `HasConflict`, clears the conflict message, and calls `CheckForConflicts`; the asynchronous response can set the conflict state back to true on every auto-repeat, so the reported blinking can continue and repeated conflict checks keep being queued. Track the last key-down hotkey state and return before the conflict reset/check path when the repeated key did not change `internalSettings`; reset that cached state on key-up and when the dialog opens.

proposed_comments.title: Keep the dependency-property setter as a real assignment
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep the dependency-property setter as a real assignment

**Severity:** `medium`

Moving the equality guard into the `Keys` dependency-property setter changes the setter's semantics: assigning an equal-but-different list leaves the old list instance in the property, so callers can read back or mutate a value different from the one they assigned. Keep the setter as the normal `SetValue` wrapper and apply duplicate-update suppression at the hotkey repeat call sites instead.

```suggestion
            get => (List<object>)GetValue(KeysProperty);
            set => SetValue(KeysProperty, value);
```

> If applying multiple suggestions in this file individually, apply the lower-line suggestion first or batch the suggestions so line shifts do not stale the later range.
